question.problem: Consider the arc of the curve $y=\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}$ that lies between the lines $x=-1$ and $x=1.$ Calculate the surface area generated when this arc is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
We can find the surface area generated when a curve is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis using the formula

$$
S=\int 2\pi y\,\text{d}s.
$$

Since we're given a curve in the form $y=f(x),$ we have 

$$
\text{d}s=\sqrt{1+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Therefore, we will use

$$
S=2\pi {\int }_{{x}_{1}}^{{x}_{2}}y\sqrt{1+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We are told that the limits of integration are from ${x}_{1}=-1$ to ${x}_{2}=1.$ 

Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}})=-\frac{x}{\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}}\,⇒\,{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})}^{2}=\frac{{x}^{2}}{4-{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =2\pi {\int }_{{x}_{1}}^{{x}_{2}}y\sqrt{1+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}\sqrt{1+\frac{{x}^{2}}{4-{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}\sqrt{\frac{4}{4-{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}2\,\text{d}x \\  & =4\pi x\,{|}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =4\pi [1-(-1)] \\  & =8\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
